faq.answer: The facet describes a general tendency. Clinical depression is assessed from the person's actual symptoms, history, circumstances, and impact on life. A personality result cannot diagnose or exclude it.
faq.question: How is the Depression facet different from clinical depression?

faq.answer: Yes. Enjoyment and low mood should be understood separately. An enjoyable moment or a cheerful public manner does not settle whether distress is significant.
faq.question: Can I enjoy things and still have significant low mood?

faq.answer: Not by itself. The loss, its meaning, and the support available are central to understanding that experience. A difficult period is not a clean measure of a general tendency.
faq.question: Does sadness after bereavement reveal my personality level?

faq.answer: The record cannot establish or promise that. Its purpose is to clarify when a particular experience occurs and what conditions accompany it. Changes after support or a routine adjustment are observations about those occasions.
faq.question: Will keeping a record change this facet?

faq.answer: No. It cannot identify an individual's genetic cause, percentage, or prognosis. A score does not provide that causal information.
faq.question: Can this result explain whether my low mood is inherited?

not_for: Do not use this page for clinical diagnosis or as the sole basis for hiring or admission.
method_boundary.summary: Use this page to understand personality concepts and examine everyday behavior. Interpret actual scores using the instrument’s scoring method, reference sample, and intended use.

sections.body:
In the NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary used on this site, Depression concerns a tendency toward low mood and discouragement, including negative feelings about oneself. The technical name does not mean that a person has a depressive disorder or that sadness defines their identity.

A tendency concerns a pattern across occasions. Feeling low today describes a state. Grieving a loss requires attention to what happened and what the person needs. Clinical depression requires an assessment beyond a personality description. These distinctions matter even when the same everyday word is used for all three.
sections.heading: A facet name is not a diagnosis

sections.body:
A stronger tendency can mean that discouragement or negative self-evaluation enters everyday experience more readily. A weaker tendency can mean that these experiences occur less often. Frequency, intensity, and duration should still be observed separately rather than assumed to rise and fall together.

Neither position measures emotional depth, creativity, kindness, resilience, or mental health. A person who usually experiences little discouragement may have a painful period or a depressive disorder. Someone with a stronger tendency may also have satisfying relationships and genuinely enjoyable experiences.

Intermediate descriptions belong to a continuum, not a separate personality type. This page does not set thresholds or prescribe a preferred score.
sections.heading: What stronger and weaker tendencies describe

sections.body:
The official [NEO/IPIP comparison table](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEO_FacetsTable.htm) places Depression at N3 and Cheerfulness, corresponding to Positive Emotions, at E6 under Extraversion. They are distinct constructs with different item content, not two names for one score reversed.

Ask about discouragement and enjoyment separately. A person may feel low about a disappointment and still enjoy music later that day. Another may be emotionally quiet without feeling sad. A cheerful manner cannot establish the absence of distress.

This is not a claim that positive and negative emotion are wholly unrelated. It is a reason to avoid inferring one unmeasured experience from the other.
sections.heading: Why enjoyment cannot be used as the opposite score

sections.body:
Imagine volunteering with a community garden. The group chooses another planting design instead of yours. You feel disappointed, then keep returning to the thought that you have nothing useful to offer. The low mood continues beyond the meeting.

Separate three questions: what the group decided, how you felt, and what you concluded about yourself. The decision may reflect cost or maintenance requirements. Neither your discouragement nor the group's choice establishes your general ability.

A natural exception would be another proposal being declined under ordinary conditions, without a planned mood exercise or special reassurance, when you felt disappointed but did not become persistently discouraged or devalue yourself broadly. It would not disprove a usual tendency. It could help narrow the explanation to particular stakes, feedback styles, or circumstances.
sections.heading: A setback, a broad conclusion, and a natural exception

sections.body:
Choose a manageable working question, such as: “After ordinary proposal feedback, do I become discouraged and draw a broad negative conclusion about myself?” Do not seek out rejection to create a test.

On relevant occasions, record the actual feedback, your reported mood, the self-evaluation that arose, and when you later noticed the feeling still present or no longer present. Note any impact on daily activities. Record enjoyment separately. Completing an activity is not proof that the mood has lifted, and missing it may have an unrelated explanation.

Include feedback occasions where the target discouragement did not occur. Days without relevant feedback offer no opportunity to observe this particular question. Failing to find a counterexample in a limited review is not evidence that exceptions never occur.

Mark intentional changes separately: asking for clearer feedback, speaking with a friend, or changing your workload alters the circumstances. Any subsequent difference may help you choose support, but it does not establish a change in personality.
sections.heading: A record that includes absence as well as presence

sections.body:
Repeated similar experiences across relevant occasions can justify retaining a modest working explanation, provided the record is not confined to one unusual period. It cannot validate a trait score.

Narrow the explanation if discouragement clusters around one kind of feedback while comparable occasions often go differently. Perhaps public decisions are harder than private comments, or a particular project matters much more. One natural exception does not erase a usual pattern; recurring differences should be reflected in its wording.

Leave a general trait interpretation open if opportunities were scarce, mood was not recorded, or a major loss or ongoing strain dominates the period. For an ordinary proposal, one useful next step is to ask which concrete requirement it did not meet. That clarifies the task; it does not require you to stop feeling disappointed.
sections.heading: Retain, narrow, or leave the question open

sections.body:
Actual distress matters more than the label. [NIMH's depression overview](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/topics/depression) describes clinical depression as involving symptoms that affect feelings, thinking, and daily activities. Persistent low mood, loss of interest, or difficulty functioning deserves a conversation with a qualified health professional. You do not need every symptom or a high personality score to ask for help.

Seek immediate support for suicidal thoughts or urges to harm yourself. In immediate danger, contact local emergency services or go to an emergency department. [NIMH's help guidance](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/my-mental-health-do-i-need-help) lists US services; readers elsewhere should use services in their location. Observation exercises should not delay support.
sections.heading: When understanding needs to include professional support

sections.body:
The official [IPIP long-form item key](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEOFacetsKey.htm) and [four-item scales](https://ipip.ori.org/30FacetNEO-PI-RItems_Maples_etal.htm) inform the N3 vocabulary. They do not establish a diagnosis, an individual's genetic explanation, or the validity of another product's score.

The [BFI-2 author page](https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~johnlab/bfi.html) describes a different facet structure. A shared Big Five framework does not make every inventory's narrower scales identical. Read the version and score explanation attached to your actual result rather than estimating an unreported Depression score from a domain score or positive-emotion result.

For the broader domain, read [Neuroticism](/en/personality/big-five/neuroticism). [Anxiety](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anxiety) helps distinguish worry from discouragement, while [Vulnerability](/en/personality/big-five/facets/vulnerability) concerns feeling unable to cope under pressure. See the [30-facet guide](/en/personality/big-five/facets) for the full vocabulary.
